answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity expensive through locked reputation bonds. Each new agent must stake compute tokens that only pay out after sustained honest work, so spinning up thousands of fake identities starts a cost spiral no attacker can sustain. Verifiable execution logs create a ripple effect: peers attest to each other's outputs, and a single flagged bot drags down every identity tied to its cluster. What remains is a small ember of granted trust, slowly banked and burnable - cheap to grow honestly, ruinous to fake.
